|------------------|------------------|

## One lesson, three notebooks

::::: columns
::: {.column width="42%"}
**The lesson:** SQL on a synthetic OMOP extract, taught through marimo's features (reactivity, SQL cells, widgets, interactive charts and tables, forms)

**The same content, three ways**, so you can compare how each tool

- **runs** your code
- handles **interactivity**
- gets **shared** with learners
:::

::: {.column width="58%"}
::: small
| Version | File | Run it |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| **Quarto deck** (marimo engine) | `sql-basics.qmd` | [slides](sql-basics.html) |
| **marimo notebook** | `sql-basics-marimo.py` | [molab](https://molab.marimo.io/github/{{< meta repo-path >}}/sql-basics-marimo.py) · [in your browser]({{< meta pages-url >}}) · [file](sql-basics-marimo.py) |
| **Jupyter notebook** | `sql-basics-jupyter.ipynb` | [Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/{{< meta repo-path >}}/sql-basics-jupyter.ipynb) · [file](sql-basics-jupyter.ipynb) |
:::

::: muted
All three have the same sections in the same order. The marimo and Jupyter notebooks add a full SQL appendix
:::
:::

```{python .marimo}
#| output: false
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Synthetic OMOP CDM v5.4 subset stored in omop.duckdb.
# Concept IDs are real standard OMOP concepts; people, dates and
# values are simulated. Rebuild with: uv run build_omop_db.py
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Resolve relative to this document, not wherever quarto was launched from.
DB_PATH = (mo.notebook_dir() or Path.cwd()) / "omop.duckdb"
if DB_PATH.exists():
    con = duckdb.connect(str(DB_PATH), read_only=True)
else:
    # In the browser (Pyodide) omop.duckdb is not on the virtual
    # filesystem, so rebuild the same seeded tables in memory.
    # Keep in sync with build_omop_db.py.
    _rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
    _N = 1200
    _t0 = pd.Timestamp("2016-01-01")
    _span = (pd.Timestamp("2024-12-31") - _t0).days

    _concept = pd.DataFrame(
        [
            (8507, "MALE", "Gender", "Gender"),
            (8532, "FEMALE", "Gender", "Gender"),
            (8527, "White", "Race", "Race"),
            (8516, "Black or African American", "Race", "Race"),
            (8515, "Asian", "Race", "Race"),
            (38003563, "Hispanic or Latino", "Ethnicity", "Ethnicity"),
            (38003564, "Not Hispanic or Latino", "Ethnicity", "Ethnicity"),
            (9201, "Inpatient Visit", "Visit", "Visit"),
            (9202, "Outpatient Visit", "Visit", "Visit"),
            (9203, "Emergency Room Visit", "Visit", "Visit"),
            (201826, "Type 2 diabetes mellitus", "Condition", "SNOMED"),
            (320128, "Essential hypertension", "Condition", "SNOMED"),
            (317576, "Coronary arteriosclerosis", "Condition", "SNOMED"),
            (255573, "Chronic obstructive lung disease", "Condition", "SNOMED"),
            (46271022, "Chronic kidney disease", "Condition", "SNOMED"),
            (433736, "Obesity", "Condition", "SNOMED"),
            (4329847, "Myocardial infarction", "Condition", "SNOMED"),
            (440383, "Depressive disorder", "Condition", "SNOMED"),
            (197320, "Acute renal failure syndrome", "Condition", "SNOMED"),
            (1503297, "metformin", "Drug", "RxNorm"),
            (1308216, "lisinopril", "Drug", "RxNorm"),
            (1545958, "atorvastatin", "Drug", "RxNorm"),
            (1112807, "aspirin", "Drug", "RxNorm"),
            (1307046, "metoprolol", "Drug", "RxNorm"),
            (1332418, "amlodipine", "Drug", "RxNorm"),
            (3004410, "Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood", "Measurement", "LOINC"),
            (3016723, "Creatinine [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma", "Measurement", "LOINC"),
            (3004249, "Systolic blood pressure", "Measurement", "LOINC"),
        ],
        columns=["concept_id", "concept_name", "domain_id", "vocabulary_id"],
    )

    # person -------------------------------------------------------------
    _person = pd.DataFrame({
        "person_id": np.arange(1, _N + 1),
        "gender_concept_id": _rng.choice([8507, 8532], _N, p=[.48, .52]),
        "year_of_birth": _rng.integers(1935, 2006, _N),
        "month_of_birth": _rng.integers(1, 13, _N),
        "race_concept_id": _rng.choice([8527, 8516, 8515, 0], _N, p=[.6, .2, .08, .12]),
        "ethnicity_concept_id": _rng.choice([38003563, 38003564], _N, p=[.25, .75]),
    })
    _age = dict(zip(_person.person_id, 2024 - _person.year_of_birth))

    # visit_occurrence ---------------------------------------------------
    _nv = (_rng.poisson(4, _N) + 1).astype(np.intp)  # np.repeat needs intp (int32 in WASM)
    _vp = np.repeat(_person.person_id.values, _nv)
    _V = len(_vp)
    _vtype = _rng.choice([9201, 9202, 9203], _V, p=[.12, .75, .13])
    _vstart = _t0 + pd.to_timedelta(_rng.integers(0, _span, _V), unit="D")
    _los = np.where(_vtype == 9201, _rng.integers(1, 11, _V), 0)
    _visit = pd.DataFrame({
        "visit_occurrence_id": np.arange(1, _V + 1),
        "person_id": _vp,
        "visit_concept_id": _vtype,
        "visit_start_date": _vstart,
        "visit_end_date": _vstart + pd.to_timedelta(_los, unit="D"),
    })
    _by_person = {p: g for p, g in _visit.groupby("person_id")}

    # condition_occurrence ------------------------------------------------
    _base = {201826: .16, 320128: .28, 317576: .09, 255573: .07, 46271022: .06,
             433736: .15, 4329847: .03, 440383: .12, 197320: .04}
    _crow = []
    for _pid, _g in _by_person.items():
        _scale = 0.35 + _age[_pid] / 55
        for _cid, _p in _base.items():
            if _rng.random() < min(_p * _scale, .85):
                _v = _g.iloc[_rng.integers(0, len(_g))]
                _crow.append((_pid, _cid, _v.visit_start_date, _v.visit_occurrence_id))
    _cond = pd.DataFrame(_crow, columns=["person_id", "condition_concept_id",
                                         "condition_start_date", "visit_occurrence_id"])
    _cond.insert(0, "condition_occurrence_id", np.arange(1, len(_cond) + 1))
    _has = _cond.groupby("person_id").condition_concept_id.apply(set).to_dict()

    # drug_exposure -------------------------------------------------------
    _drow = []
    for _pid, _g in _by_person.items():
        _cs = _has.get(_pid, set())
        if 201826 in _cs and _rng.random() < .72:
            _d0 = _cond[(_cond.person_id == _pid) & (_cond.condition_concept_id == 201826)].condition_start_date.iloc[0]
            _drow.append((_pid, 1503297, _d0 + pd.Timedelta(days=int(_rng.integers(0, 240)))))
        if 320128 in _cs:
            for _dc in (1308216, 1332418):
                if _rng.random() < .45:
                    _drow.append((_pid, _dc, _g.visit_start_date.iloc[_rng.integers(0, len(_g))]))
        if _cs & {317576, 4329847}:
            for _dc in (1545958, 1112807, 1307046):
                if _rng.random() < .6:
                    _drow.append((_pid, _dc, _g.visit_start_date.iloc[_rng.integers(0, len(_g))]))
    _drug = pd.DataFrame(_drow, columns=["person_id", "drug_concept_id", "drug_exposure_start_date"])
    _drug["days_supply"] = _rng.choice([30, 90], len(_drug))
    _drug["drug_exposure_end_date"] = _drug.drug_exposure_start_date + pd.to_timedelta(_drug.days_supply, unit="D")
    _drug.insert(0, "drug_exposure_id", np.arange(1, len(_drug) + 1))

    # measurement ---------------------------------------------------------
    _mrow = []
    for _v in _visit.itertuples():
        _cs = _has.get(_v.person_id, set())
        if _rng.random() < .35:
            _a1c = _rng.normal(7.9, 1.3) if 201826 in _cs else _rng.normal(5.4, .35)
            _mrow.append((_v.person_id, 3004410, _v.visit_start_date, round(max(_a1c, 4.0), 1), "%"))
        if _rng.random() < .6:
            _cr = _rng.lognormal(0, .2) * (1.9 if 197320 in _cs and _rng.random() < .5 else 1.0)
            _cr *= 1.35 if 46271022 in _cs else 1.0
            _mrow.append((_v.person_id, 3016723, _v.visit_start_date, round(_cr, 2), "mg/dL"))
        if _rng.random() < .8:
            _sbp = _rng.normal(141 if 320128 in _cs else 122, 13)
            _mrow.append((_v.person_id, 3004249, _v.visit_start_date, round(_sbp), "mmHg"))
    _meas = pd.DataFrame(_mrow, columns=["person_id", "measurement_concept_id",
                                         "measurement_date", "value_as_number", "unit_source_value"])
    _meas.insert(0, "measurement_id", np.arange(1, len(_meas) + 1))

    # load into DuckDB with proper DATE columns ---------------------------
    con = duckdb.connect()
    for _name, _df in {"person": _person, "visit_occurrence": _visit,
                       "condition_occurrence": _cond, "drug_exposure": _drug,
                       "measurement": _meas, "concept": _concept}.items():
        con.register("_tmp", _df)
        _cols = ", ".join(
            f"CAST({c} AS DATE) AS {c}" if c.endswith("_date") else c for c in _df.columns
        )
        con.execute(f"CREATE TABLE {_name} AS SELECT {_cols} FROM _tmp")
        con.unregister("_tmp")


def run(q):
    """Run SQL against the OMOP connection and return a pandas DataFrame."""
    return con.execute(q).df()


def show_sql(q):
    return mo.md(f"```sql\n{q.strip()}\n```")


CLAUSE = {"select": "#0021A5", "from": "#002657", "where": "#C63A0E",
          "join": "#6A2A60", "group": "#22884C", "having": "#7A5C00",
          "order": "#D32737", "window": "#343741",
          "ink": "#1A1A1A", "muted": "#5F6168"}


def styled(chart, w=520, h=300):
    return (chart.properties(width=w, height=h)
            .configure(font="Georgia")
            .configure_view(stroke=None)
            .configure_axis(labelColor=CLAUSE["ink"], titleColor=CLAUSE["muted"],
                            gridColor="#E6E7E6", domainColor="#C7C9C8",
                            labelFontSize=13, titleFontSize=13)
            .configure_legend(labelFontSize=13, titleFontSize=13))
```

## Why another notebook?

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
Jupyter notebooks are great for exploring, but the notebook you **see** is not always the program that **runs**

- Cells can be run in **any order**
- Deleting a cell **doesn't delete** its variables
- Widgets only update the cell they live in
- `.ipynb` is JSON with outputs inside, so **git diffs are noisy**

::: muted
For teaching, that means a student's notebook can show results that its code no longer produces
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
> In a study of ~1.4 million GitHub notebooks, only **24%** ran without errors and only **4%** reproduced their saved results
>
> Pimentel et al., *MSR 2019*

::: muted
marimo's answer: make the notebook a **reactive program**. Each cell declares what it reads and defines, and marimo keeps every output consistent with the code
:::
:::
:::::

## Hidden state, live

This slide runs marimo on the lesson's HbA1c results. **Move cell A**, then compare the two notebooks

:::::: columns
:::: {.column width="38%"}
```{python .marimo}
#| output: false
hba1c = run("""
SELECT value_as_number FROM measurement
WHERE measurement_concept_id = 3004410
""").value_as_number.to_numpy()
get_snap, set_snap = mo.state(6.5)
```

```{python .marimo}
thr = mo.ui.slider(4.0, 10.0, value=6.5, step=0.5, label="Cell A: threshold =",
                   show_value=True, full_width=True)
thr
```

```{python .marimo}
rerun_b = mo.ui.button(label="▶ Run cell B in Jupyter",
                       on_click=lambda _: set_snap(thr.value), kind="warn")
rerun_b
```

::: muted
- **Jupyter:** cell B only reruns when you run it
- **marimo:** cell B reruns as soon as `threshold` changes

The Jupyter notebook has this as a hands-on exercise
:::
::::

::: {.column width="62%"}
```{python .marimo}
_stale = get_snap() != thr.value
_n_old = int((hba1c >= get_snap()).sum())
_n_new = int((hba1c >= thr.value).sum())
_code = (
    "```python\n"
    f"# A\nthreshold = {thr.value}\n\n"
    "# B\nn_flagged = (hba1c >= threshold).sum()\n\n"
    "# C\nprint(f\"{n_flagged} HbA1c results ≥ {threshold}%\")\n"
    "```"
)
mo.vstack([
    mo.md(_code),
    mo.hstack([
        mo.callout(mo.md(
            f"**Jupyter** · cell C prints\n\n`{_n_old} HbA1c results ≥ {thr.value}%`\n\n"
            + (f"⚠️ B last ran with threshold = {get_snap()}" if _stale else "✓ in sync")),
            kind="danger" if _stale else "success"),
        mo.callout(mo.md(
            f"**marimo** · cell C prints\n\n`{_n_new} HbA1c results ≥ {thr.value}%`\n\n"
            "✓ always in sync"), kind="success"),
    ], widths=[1, 1], gap=1),
])
```
:::
::::::

## How marimo runs a notebook

::::: columns
::: {.column width="44%"}
marimo reads each cell's code to find the **names it defines** and the **names it reads**. That gives a dependency graph

- Change a cell → marimo reruns **everything that depends on it**, and nothing else
- Each global name is defined in **one** cell
- Delete a cell → its variables are **deleted** too
- UI elements (`mo.ui.*`) are just variables, so interacting with one reruns the cells that read `.value`
:::

::: {.column width="56%"}
```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 7
flowchart TD
    data["<b>data cell</b><br/>con, run()"]
    ui["<b>widget cell</b><br/>yob = mo.ui.range_slider()"]
    sql["<b>SQL cell</b><br/>where_df = mo.sql(...)"]
    chain["<b>SQL cell</b><br/>SELECT … FROM where_df"]
    chart["<b>chart cell</b><br/>reads where_df"]
    data --> sql
    ui --> sql
    sql --> chain
    sql --> chart
    style ui fill:#FA4616,color:#fff,stroke:#FA4616
    style sql fill:#0021A5,color:#fff,stroke:#0021A5
    style chain fill:#0021A5,color:#fff,stroke:#0021A5
    style chart fill:#0021A5,color:#fff,stroke:#0021A5
```

::: muted
Move the slider (orange) and only the blue cells rerun
:::
:::
:::::

## How each notebook is structured

::: panel-tabset
### Quarto `.qmd`

````markdown
---
engine: marimo
pyproject: |
  dependencies = ["marimo[sql]", "duckdb", "altair"]
---

## UI elements and `.value`

```{python .marimo}
#| echo: true
yob = mo.ui.range_slider(1935, 2005, value=[1950, 1975], label="Year of birth")
yob
```
````

::: muted
Markdown with code blocks. Quarto owns the layout (slides, columns, theme); `engine: marimo` makes the blocks reactive cells that run in the browser
:::

### marimo `.py`

```python
# /// script
# dependencies = ["marimo[sql]", "duckdb", "altair"]
# ///
import marimo
app = marimo.App(css_file="omop-marimo.css")

@app.cell
def _(mo):
    yob = mo.ui.range_slider(1935, 2005, value=[1950, 1975], label="Year of birth")
    yob
    return (yob,)

@app.cell
def _(con, mo, yob):
    where_df = mo.sql(f"""
        SELECT person_id FROM person
        WHERE year_of_birth BETWEEN {yob.value[0]} AND {yob.value[1]}
    """, engine=con)
    return (where_df,)
```

::: muted
Plain Python. Each cell is a function: its arguments are what it reads, its `return` is what it defines. Git-friendly, importable, and it runs with `python file.py`
:::

### Jupyter `.ipynb`

```json
{
 "cell_type": "code",
 "execution_count": 7,
 "metadata": {},
 "outputs": [
  {"data": {"text/html": "<div><table border=\"1\" class=\"dataframe\">…"},
   "execution_count": 7, "output_type": "execute_result"}
 ],
 "source": ["@w.interact(yob=w.IntRangeSlider(value=(1950, 1975), …))\n",
            "def where_demo(yob):\n", "    display(run(sql))"]
}
```

::: muted
JSON, with outputs and execution counts saved inside. Re-running a cell changes the file even when the code didn't change
:::
:::

## How each notebook runs

::::: columns
::: {.column width="33%"}
### Quarto

``` bash
quarto preview sql-basics.qmd
```

- Renders to **static HTML** with interactive **islands**
- Python runs in the viewer's browser (**Pyodide**)
- Viewers can't edit the code

[Open the deck](sql-basics.html)
:::

::: {.column width="34%"}
### marimo

``` bash
uvx marimo edit --sandbox \
  sql-basics-marimo.py
```

- A **real kernel** (local or molab), or the **browser**
- The same file is a notebook, an **app** (`marimo run`) or a script
- Learners edit and rerun everything

[molab](https://molab.marimo.io/github/{{< meta repo-path >}}/sql-basics-marimo.py) · [in your browser]({{< meta pages-url >}})
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
### Jupyter

``` bash
uv run --with jupyterlab … \
  jupyter lab sql-basics-jupyter.ipynb
```

- An IPython **kernel**; you run cells by hand
- Widgets via **ipywidgets** callbacks
- Huge ecosystem; Colab, Binder

[Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/{{< meta repo-path >}}/sql-basics-jupyter.ipynb)
:::
:::::

## Live: widgets drive a query

::::: columns
::: {.column width="56%"}
```{python .marimo}
ex_yob = mo.ui.range_slider(1935, 2005, value=[1950, 1975], step=1,
                            label="Year of birth", show_value=True, full_width=True)
ex_sex = mo.ui.dropdown({"Anyone": 0, "Female": 8532, "Male": 8507},
                        value="Anyone", label="Sex")
mo.hstack([ex_yob, ex_sex], widths=[3, 1], gap=1.5, align="end")
```

```{python .marimo}
_sex_sql = "" if ex_sex.value == 0 else f"\n  AND gender_concept_id = {ex_sex.value}"
_sql = f"""
SELECT person_id, gender_concept_id, year_of_birth
FROM person
WHERE year_of_birth BETWEEN {ex_yob.value[0]} AND {ex_yob.value[1]}{_sex_sql}
"""
_df = run(_sql)
mo.vstack([
    show_sql(_sql),
    mo.md(f"**{len(_df):,}** people match · `ex_yob.value = {tuple(ex_yob.value)}`"),
    mo.ui.table(_df, page_size=4, selection=None),
])
```

ex_lab = mo.ui.dropdown(

    value="HbA1c (%)", label="Lab")

```{python .marimo}
_cid, _lo, _hi, _default = ex_lab.value
ex_cutoff = mo.ui.slider(_lo, _hi, value=_default, step=0.1 if _hi < 20 else 1,
                         label="Abnormal if ≥", show_value=True, full_width=True)
mo.hstack([ex_lab, ex_cutoff], widths=[1, 2], gap=1.5, align="end")
```

```{python .marimo}
_m = run(f"""
SELECT value_as_number,
       CASE WHEN value_as_number >= {ex_cutoff.value}
            THEN 'abnormal' ELSE 'normal' END AS flag
FROM measurement
WHERE measurement_concept_id = {ex_lab.value[0]}
  AND value_as_number IS NOT NULL
""")
_pct = (_m.flag == "abnormal").mean() * 100 if len(_m) else 0
_h = alt.Chart(_m).mark_bar().encode(
    x=alt.X("value_as_number:Q", bin=alt.Bin(maxbins=40), title=None),
    y=alt.Y("count():Q", title="results"),
    color=alt.Color("flag:N", scale=alt.Scale(domain=["abnormal", "normal"],
                                               range=[CLAUSE["order"], "#B3BCE3"]),
                    legend=alt.Legend(orient="top", title=None)),
)
_rule = alt.Chart(pd.DataFrame({"x": [ex_cutoff.value]})).mark_rule(
    color=CLAUSE["ink"], strokeDash=[5, 4], strokeWidth=2).encode(x="x:Q")
mo.vstack([mo.md(f"**{_pct:.1f}%** of {len(_m):,} results flagged abnormal"),
           styled(_h + _rule, w=560, h=200)])
```

### Jupyter

``` python
def reset_slider(change):
    _, lo, hi, default = LABS[change["new"]]
    with cutoff.hold_trait_notifications():
        cutoff.min, cutoff.max = lo, hi
        cutoff.value = default
    draw_lab()

lab_pick.observe(reset_slider, names="value")
cutoff.observe(draw_lab, names="value")
```

Callbacks, an `Output` widget, and care with `min` / `max`

## Live: click a chart, query the selection

::::: columns
::: {.column width="56%"}
**Click a bar** (shift-click for several)

```{python .marimo}
_bands = run("""
SELECT CASE
         WHEN 2024 - year_of_birth < 40 THEN '18–39'
         WHEN 2024 - year_of_birth < 65 THEN '40–64'
         ELSE '65+'
       END AS age_band,
       COUNT(*) AS people
FROM person
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
""")
# No cornerRadiusEnd here: combined with a selection, marimo islands draw the bars invisible.
ex_age_chart = mo.ui.altair_chart(
    styled(alt.Chart(_bands).mark_bar(color=CLAUSE["select"]).encode(
        x=alt.X("age_band:N", title=None, axis=alt.Axis(labelAngle=0)),
        y=alt.Y("people:Q", title="people"),
    ), w=300, h=220),
    chart_selection="point",
)
```

```{python .marimo}
_sel = ex_age_chart.value
_picked = sorted(_sel["age_band"].unique()) if len(_sel) else ["18–39", "40–64", "65+"]
_in = ", ".join(f"'{b}'" for b in _picked)
_top = run(f"""
WITH banded AS (
  SELECT person_id,
         CASE WHEN 2024 - year_of_birth < 40 THEN '18–39'
              WHEN 2024 - year_of_birth < 65 THEN '40–64'
              ELSE '65+' END AS age_band
  FROM person
)
SELECT c.concept_name AS condition, COUNT(DISTINCT b.person_id) AS patients
FROM banded AS b
JOIN condition_occurrence AS co ON b.person_id = co.person_id
JOIN concept AS c ON co.condition_concept_id = c.concept_id
WHERE b.age_band IN ({_in})
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5
""")
mo.hstack([
    ex_age_chart,
    mo.vstack([mo.md(f"Selected: **{', '.join(_picked)}**"),
               mo.ui.table(_top, selection=None, page_size=5)]),
], widths=[1, 1], gap=1)
```

## Side by side

::: small
|  | Quarto + marimo | Native marimo | Jupyter |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| **File** | `.qmd` (Markdown) | `.py` (Python) | `.ipynb` (JSON + outputs) |
| **Execution** | Reactive | Reactive | Manual, any order |
| **Hidden state** | No | No | Yes |
| **Widgets across cells** | Automatic | Automatic | Callbacks |
| **SQL** | `{sql .marimo}` blocks | SQL cells → DataFrames | Strings in Python (or `%%sql`) |
| **Clickable tables / charts** | Charts (tables display only) | Both | Charts via `JupyterChart`; no built-in table |
| **Where Python runs** | Pyodide in the browser | Local kernel, molab, or Pyodide | Local or remote kernel |
| **Learners can edit** | No | Yes | Yes (with a kernel) |
| **Git diffs** | Clean | Clean | Noisy |
| **Share as** | Static website | molab link, WASM page, app | Colab, Binder, nbviewer |
| **Best for** | Lecture decks, course sites | Labs, reproducible analyses, apps | Ad-hoc exploration, existing ecosystem |
:::

## Sharing with learners

::::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
**molab**: marimo's hosted notebooks, like Colab for marimo

``` text
https://molab.marimo.io/github/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<branch>/<file>.py
```

- Opens any notebook on GitHub
- Add `/wasm` to run it in the viewer's browser, with no login

**GitHub Pages**: a static site that runs Python in the browser

``` bash
uvx marimo export html-wasm sql-basics-marimo.py \
  -o docs/marimo --mode run
```

::: muted
Add an empty `.nojekyll` at the root of the Pages site, or files starting with `_` go missing
:::
:::

flowchart LR
    ipynb["sql-basics-jupyter.ipynb"]

## Which one, when?

::::: columns
::: {.column width="33%"}
### Quarto

- You're **presenting** or publishing
- You need full control of layout and theme
- Readers should see results, not edit code
:::

::: {.column width="34%"}
### marimo

- Learners should **run and change** the analysis
- You want reproducible, git-friendly notebooks
- The notebook should also work as an **app**
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
### Jupyter

- You're **exploring** on your own
- You need a Jupyter-only extension or kernel (R, Julia)
- Your platform already runs on `.ipynb`
:::
:::::

::: muted
For this course: **teach from the Quarto deck**, **practise in the marimo notebook**, and use the Jupyter version to see what reactivity saves you
:::

1. **Quarto:** open the [SQL deck](sql-basics.html) and move a few widgets
2. **marimo:** open [`sql-basics-marimo.py` on molab](https://molab.marimo.io/github/{{< meta repo-path >}}/sql-basics-marimo.py) (or [in your browser]({{< meta pages-url >}})), then
    - click a row in the *Interactive tables* section and watch the drill-down update
    - add a SQL cell that queries `where_df`
    - delete a cell and see what happens to the cells that used it
3. **Jupyter:** open [`sql-basics-jupyter.ipynb` in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/{{< meta repo-path >}}/sql-basics-jupyter.ipynb) and do the **hidden state** exercise in Part 1
